cd ~/.claude/projects/-Users-rashford-Library-Mobile-Documents-com-apple-CloudDocs-Developer-Float
for f in 0dda4d9e-6cbb-4a12-a541-fd4d105b1afb 91f97990-fd6a-498a-8132-75d96bbe424e d5dcae32-a59b-4e0b-85b0-602d09dc6767 19897670-0076-47bc-8cc8-e8e4ae343086 4c9cc721-5724-42f9-a940-eda05f06f4db; do
  echo "=== $f ==="
  head -1 "$f.jsonl" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print('type:', d.get('type'), '| summary:', d.get('summary',''))" 2>/dev/null
  # first real user message
  python3 - "$f.jsonl" <<'EOF'
import json,sys
first=None; last=None; n=0
for line in open(sys.argv[1]):
    try: d=json.loads(line)
    except: continue
    if d.get('type')=='user':
        m=d.get('message',{}); c=m.get('content')
        if isinstance(c,str): txt=c
        elif isinstance(c,list): txt=' '.join(x.get('text','') for x in c if isinstance(x,dict) and x.get('type')=='text')
        else: txt=''
        txt=txt.strip()
        if txt and not txt.startswith('<') and 'tool_result' not in str(m.get('content'))[:20]:
            if first is None: first=txt[:200]
            last=txt[:200]; n+=1
    if 'timestamp' in d: ts=d['timestamp']
print('first user msg:', first)
print('last user msg:', last)
print('user msgs:', n, '| last ts:', ts)
EOF
done

I found your recent sessions. There were two large sessions in this Float project active until just minutes ago, and one of them is almost certainly the one you closed:

1. **`0dda4d9e`** — topic: pulling raw SPHEREx data to build your own equirect 360 starfield images. Last activity **10:16 AM** (moments before this session started); the last message was an image/screenshot of a 2048×1024 render.
2. **`91f97990`** — topic: triaging the new Float images that "looked flat/grainy"; you'd built a triage page and the last message was you asking to remove the first batch you'd selected and update the page. Last activity **10:14 AM**.

Older ones from this morning (probably not what you mean): `d5dcae32` (Ollama on sdf1 timing out, ended 9:29) and `4c9cc721` (the "read the handoff, get the rest of the images on here" session, ended with a /handoff at 8:22).

The quickest way to tell which you lost: look at whichever Claude Code window is still open — if it's showing the image-triage conversation, then the closed one is the SPHEREx session, and vice versa. To reopen it, run in a terminal in this project directory:

```
claude --resume 0dda4d9e-6cbb-4a12-a541-fd4d105b1afb
```

or

```
claude --resume 91f97990-fd6a-498a-8132-75d96bbe424e
```

(You can also just run `claude --resume` with no ID to get an interactive picker showing these sessions.) Nothing was lost either way — both transcripts are fully saved on disk through their last message.

That's the image-triage session — you'd built a triage page for the new backdrops and had just asked to remove the first batch you selected. To pick it back up, open a new terminal (not inside this session) in the Float directory and run:

```
claude --resume 91f97990-fd6a-498a-8132-75d96bbe424e
```

It'll resume exactly where it left off, with your last request ("remove those and update the page") already answered or in progress — check the tail of the conversation once it opens to see whether the triage page update finished before the window closed.
